title: How to Track Squarespace Forms in GTM, and the Name Bug I Found Testing
intro:
I tested my Squarespace listener on a real contact form, with the submission request stubbed so no lead would be sent. The event fired. The email was right, and so was the phone. Then I opened the name fields, and they were empty.

Squarespace splits a Name field into two parts, and my code labelled them Name First and Name Last. The part that sorts fields didn't recognise those labels. So a tracking check that stopped at "it fired" would have passed, and every lead would have gone to Enhanced Conversions without a name.

I fixed it, retested on the same form, and both names came through. Here's the setup, from a real container with the names removed.
tldr: This free script counts a Squarespace lead when Squarespace confirms it received the form, so Squarespace design changes are less likely to break it. After you install it, send one test lead and check the name, email and phone. Seeing that it fired isn't enough.
sections: Why the usual methods fall short

Squarespace has no public success event for its form block, and its class names are hashed. So this listener watches the form's own request instead:

What happensSignalec_detection_method
Squarespace accepts the leadA 2xx from /api/form/confirmation_event
The submission message rendersThe block's message appearsSuccess path, inferred if the request wasn't seen
The form redirectspagehide on the form page, plus recall on arrivalSuccess path, using stored data
A field is marked invalidaria-invalid or .field-error after interactionsquarespace_form_failed

First Page's guide is the clearest I found. It covers thank-you pages, button clicks, a success message selector and a post-submit script that pushes an event with the form ID. That script is a good free option for a count. It has to be added to each form, and it doesn't give you contact data.

1. Download the GTM tag, or get it from GitHub.
  2. Paste it into a new Custom HTML tag, triggered on All Pages.

Load GTM as early as you can, through Squarespace's Code Injection header, because the listener has to be in place before the first submission.

Don't run this next to the universal listener. Pick one. If the site has other form tools, use the universal listener walkthrough, which is what this account does.

Create a Custom Event trigger on squarespace_form_success. Add a Page Hostname condition if the account also has landing pages elsewhere, like this one.

[[img:sqs-trigger|Website leads only.]]
Step 3: Send it to Google Ads and GA4

Attach your conversion tag to the trigger.

[[img:sqs-gads-tag|The website conversion, separate from the landing page one.]]

Send form details to GA4. For Enhanced Conversions, map ec_email, ec_phone, ec_first_name and ec_last_name in a User-Provided Data variable. The Gravity Forms walkthrough shows how to check them.

Want these in reports? GA4 won't show them until you register each one as a custom dimension. Here's how.

1. In Preview, load the form page and expect ec_tracker_initialized.
  2. Submit a labelled test lead. Expect one squarespace_form_success.
  3. Open the event and check all the ec_* values, including the name fields.
  4. Testing again? The listener ignores a repeat from the same form and person for 5 minutes, so wait or use a different email.

Then remove old click or thank-you triggers, or each lead counts twice.

• I tested the current build on a live Squarespace form with the request stubbed, so no lead was sent. A simulated 400 didn't fire. A simulated 200 fired once, with the right email, phone and names.
  • That means Squarespace's real server response wasn't part of this test. Do one labelled test lead on your own form.
  • The redirect path wasn't tested on a live form.
  • The listener only inspects requests to /api/form/. Other calls pass through untouched.

Do I need a thank-you page to track Squarespace forms?

No. The listener confirms the submission from Squarespace's own form response, so it works with the standard submission message.

How do I add Google Tag Manager to Squarespace?

Add the GTM snippet through Code Injection, then add this listener as a Custom HTML tag inside GTM. Check that your plan includes Code Injection.
